newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks meander in slow trade to close off.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks meander in slow trade to close off.

text.p: Mexican stocks slid down at the close Tuesday on lack of volume and scant investor interest.
"The market was dull, there were no foreign dealers and most dealing was in same-day buy-sell trades," said one analyst.
The blue-chip IPC index closed down 28.06 points, or 0.84 percent, at 3,307.06. Volume was a lukewarm 63.6 million shares traded.
Another analyst said market activity was slow due to holiday season.
"The market isn't reacting to any news, not Zedillo's trip to New York nor even changes in accountancy procedures. It's holiday time and everyone wants to party," said another analyst.
President Ernesto Zedillo met with U.S. businessmen and bankers in New York on Monday.

Mexico's National Banking and Securities Commission said during the session it would bring Mexican accountancy practices more in line with international procedure on schedule in January. Traders noted this would force many banks to increase their estimates of past-due loans portfolios.
On the broad market, 96 stocks were traded, of which losers trounced gainers by 61 to 14.
Steelmakers Ahmsa headed the gainers, up 80 centavos (10 cents) to 16.80 pesos ($2.14), after news the firm was to price $85 million in convertible notes, traders said.
Debt-ridden holding company Sidek led the losers after ending off 13 centavos (2 cents) at 82 centavos (10 cents).
